I4.findings: 1/ (ambiguity, resend risk) The 'Before sending' paragraph first defines a match as a message 'that does what the action asks (... the answer to that question)' and says 'unrelated mail is not a match', then defines the unique-match/candidate count without that content test. Neither A ('quick check, any thoughts on this?') nor B ('following up here, lmk') contains the audience numbers, so a reader who applies the content filter first finds zero matches for the reply action and sends the reply. If A or B was really a failed attempt at that reply, that is a near-duplicate. I followed 'Two or more such candidates, or one you can't tie to the action: HOLD' (both are unlogged messages from us to Payal on the thread since 09:30), which matches the intent. Fix: say that an unlogged message from us since the raise always counts as a candidate unless it clearly serves another logged action. 2/ STEP 1's 'unanswered' test has the same split: A/B don't answer the question, so the thread is selected here, unlike I3. 3/ One pair of mails gives Akshay two near-identical hold segments, one per action. Correct per the text, but the decision inbox would read better with one combined ask when the candidate sets are the same. 4/ The HOLD rule doesn't say what happens to the held action's own Zoya segment and owner (kept, so Zoya stays in Waiting on), or that later runs skip a held action until Your call. Each FAST/SLOW run will redo the check and hold again, which is idempotent only if WRITE PATH dedupes the identical segment and note line. 5/ SLOW's STEP 2 skip rule ('Skip a row while Akshay or Jaya holds a decision on this pursuit') does not clearly cover FAST's review hold. I treated it as a separate ask ('an independent ask of theirs ... doesn't stop a due step of yours on another obligation'), so SLOW does its own check and holds.
